threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You carry an umbrella but forget to check the weather app—it’s classic newbie. Locals embrace the drizzle like it's part of the vibe.
Last night on the 47, a bloke serenaded the whole bus with off-key 90s hits. By the time we reached Canada Water, half the passengers were in on it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a neighbor feeding the pigeons while wearing a bathrobe and slippers, I knew I was home in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a club that serves currywurst at 3 am alongside techno—no cover charge but you'll need to share a table with locals.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their casual disdain for BART delays—only a true San Franciscan knows that complaining is half the commute.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 Balboa at the wrong time—packed to the brim with people pretending not to notice the guy loudly debating with himself in the back.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think all bars serve tapas until midnight. Meanwhile, locals know to hit them up before 10 PM for the real deal, then it's just drinks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell the newcomers by their Google Maps struggle at the intersections—taking photos of every 'secret' street they find.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 'Late Night' sign at the bus stop means the buses run late, not just that they’re too busy to care.
Spotted a couple sharing a pizza on the back seat of the 133, but the real twist? They barely said a word. Just smiled and ate.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Hearing the distinct sound of 'Karaoke Night' seeping through my window at 2 AM made me realize I'm really part of this wild Neukölln tapestry.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip chai from a Turkish café while catching up on the latest graffiti art collaborations happening on the walls nearby.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by how they know to avoid the 14 Mission after 5 PM—it's not just packed, it’s a meltdown with that BART delay chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus that broke down by Civic Center. Everyone spilled out, and for a moment it was like an unplanned street fair—people sharing stories, laughing.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí. The real gems are the tiny plazas where locals sip vermut and chat, far from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they still order 'tapas' like it's a menu item instead of asking for 'una ronda' at the bar.
